solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Covering for apprentices, principal always ready to experiment

indicators.note: to experiment is to try things out in new ways, so the letters are tried in a new order
principal means chief or leading, so the leading letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A head teacher is always keen to try out new ideas while standing in for the trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering for' reads as standing in for someone; here 'Covering' is a floor covering and 'for' is a link. The apprentices' letters plus A and R make the rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug woven in Iran is a classic floor covering.

clue.text: Thatcher's opt out as taken away and amended goes up in smoke

indicators.note: taken away tells us the letters of the word as are to be removed from the pool
amended means corrected or altered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's withdrawal from a treaty, once revised, comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of THATCHERS OPTOUT, remove A and S ('taken away'), and rearrange ('amended') the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something on fire so it burns away is to make it go up in flames.

clue.text: Note the difficulty with gym so choose again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
ado means fuss or trouble
PT, physical training, was the old name for school gym lessons

explanation.surface: A memo about trouble at the gym leads someone to pick a fresh option.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt something a second time is to select it once more.

clue.text: Not in the mainstream, country changed at last

indicators.note: the final letter of the country's name is swapped for another letter

parts.note: India is a country in South Asia

explanation.surface: A nation finally altered its course away from the conventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed at last' replaces the final A of INDIA with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie describes independent music or film made outside the major commercial labels and studios.

clue.text: Reformed character born to have work they distributed

parts.note: ne is French for born, used of a man's original name
op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of they are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A newborn is handed tasks that others shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges THEY into HYTE. 'Reformed' suggests an anagram but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a new convert to a faith, someone whose character has been changed.

clue.text: See 1
Wherein Incas in olden times were trying their luck

definitions.text: Wherein Incas in olden times were trying their luck

indicators.note: wherein means inside which, so the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: A historical image of South American people gambling long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across incAS IN Olden; the whole clue also describes a gambling house.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is a place where people try their luck at games of chance.

clue.text: Mean to nail it perfectly after retreating somewhat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the run is read from right to left
somewhat means partly, so only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: Advice to hammer something in exactly right before backing off a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes NAILITPER from 'nail it perfectly'; 'retreating' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptilian is used of a person who is cold, sly and nasty, i.e. mean.

clue.text: Irishman in the river! One goes in as well to make amends!

indicators.note: in places the Irishman inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite crossword river

indicators.note: goes in puts the letter for one inside the Irishman's name

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is a stock Irish name in crosswords
the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: An Irishman falls into a river, and someone else jumps in too to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation marks dress up a comic accident; 'One goes in as well' means a second figure, the numeral, joins the Irishman inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to atone for it, making amends.

clue.text: Sailor 'e caught with disease ended early signs of distress

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so the sailor holds the dropped-aitch pronoun

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
'e is he with the h dropped, giving just the letter E

indicators.note: ended early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: dropsy is an old name for oedema, fluid swelling

explanation.surface: A Cockney sailor fell ill and his life ended too soon, prompting grief.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR holds E to make TEAR; DROPSY loses its final Y ('ended early').
explanation.definitionFit: Tears running down the face are visible signs that someone is upset.

clue.text: Youngster at work backing type of children's book

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for work is reversed

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a pup is a young animal, and also a cheeky youth

explanation.surface: A young person at a job is supporting a particular kind of book for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up book has pictures that stand up when the pages open, a children's favourite.

clue.text: Thousand smackers, non-stop and without reserve? Could be, playing this game!

indicators.note: without says the letters for reserve are subtracted from the pool
playing about with letters means shuffling them into a new order

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, as in £10K
the word non-stop taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A party game where a thousand kisses are given constantly and with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool K + SMACKERS + NONSTOP, remove R, E, S ('without reserve'), and rearrange ('playing'). Smackers is slang for kisses, fitting the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman's knock is a party game in which players pay for imaginary letters with kisses.

clue.text: Fresh air in Oslo's premier district

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letter of the city's name is taken

parts.note: a zone is a district or area

explanation.surface: Clean air in the best part of the Norwegian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is informal for fresh, invigorating air, especially at the seaside.

clue.text: Talked of practical headgear and its disadvantages

indicators.note: talked of means spoken, so the words are said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: handy means practical and caps are headgear

explanation.surface: A discussion of useful hats and their drawbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Handicaps are obstacles or burdens that put someone at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Shorts and top adjusted in Hampshire

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word inside the county abbreviation

parts.note: Hants is the standard abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters of top are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone altered their shorts and top while in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast; its short form is standard in postal addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot pants are very short, tight shorts fashionable in the 1970s.

clue.text: Runt?

parts.note: the clue word, read as an instruction, is a word for turn with its letters rearranged about

explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of RUNT are TURN shuffled about, so the clue itself shows what the phrase describes: a word for turn put the other way about.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a complete reversal of direction, which is what the clue word shows.

clue.text: Plume one rearranged on top of bird's head

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a different order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: A feather is repositioned on the crown of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pileum is the ornithological term for the crown of a bird's head.

clue.text: Perfect score — 10 — is common knowledge

indicators.note: to perfect something is to correct and refine it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: 10 spelt out is ten

explanation.surface: A perfect score of ten is widely known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' looks like an adjective for the score but is the anagram signal, working on SCORE and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is no secret is known by everyone.

clue.text: Go quietly, putting an end to drug

parts.note: a tip is an end or point
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Moving softly, someone stops taking a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk on the toes so as to make no noise.

clue.text: Father takes a drink if heading north — it's hot stuff

indicators.note: takes means holds in, so the father's name contains the drink

parts.note: papa is a word for father

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Dad has a drink when going up north: it's spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' works because this is a down entry, read upwards; 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a hot spice made from ground peppers.

clue.text: Origin of the jet

definitions.meaning: a spout or spray of water shooting upwards

explanation.definitionFit: Fountain means both a spring or source and an ornamental jet of water.

clue.text: Simultaneously wonderful and dreadful

definitions.meaning: in its older sense, inspiring dread and fear

explanation.surface: Something is great and terrible at the same moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome means inspiring awe, which can be either admiration or fear, and informally excellent.

clue.text: Boy Wonder loses his head, taking degree as a witchdoctor

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the trimmed name contains the degree
loses his head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Robin, Batman's sidekick, is called the Boy Wonder
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Batman's sidekick is beheaded and gains a qualification as a sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boy Wonder is Batman's young partner in the comics; obeah is a Caribbean folk religion.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi-man is a practitioner of obeah, a Caribbean folk magic, so a kind of sorcerer.

clue.text: Trustworthy delegate you said supports the board

parts.note: a rep is a representative or delegate

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so the word is heard as a letter

parts.note: the word you, which spoken sounds like the letter U
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A dependable representative, you said, backs the company directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputable person has a good name and can be trusted.

clue.text: Second mountain express

parts.note: a peak is a mountain top

explanation.surface: A fast train runs past a second mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To express something is to put it into words.

clue.text: South Pole is stormy, so decamp

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The weather at the bottom of the world is wild, so the expedition leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: To slope off is British slang for leaving quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Slope, as in slope off, means to slip away, i.e. to leave hastily.

clue.text: Holidays start and I keep us initially amused with this ode

indicators.note: start means the beginning, so the first letter of the word is taken
initially means at the beginning, so the first letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A short poem written on holiday keeps a family entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem, here loosely called an ode.

clue.text: Historic trader in sheep

definitions.meaning: the Venetian merchant who travelled to China in the 13th century
a wild Central Asian sheep with huge spiralling horns, named after the traveller

explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian explorer gave his name to a long-horned wild sheep of the Pamirs.

clue.text: New pine kitchen a shambles — that's aggravating!

indicators.note: a shambles is a complete mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moans that their newly fitted pine kitchen is a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the kitchen; it gives N, which is jumbled with PINE, KITCHEN and A by 'shambles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the neck is an irritating person or thing, something annoying.
